title: Permission matrix (Setup / Studio Access): readScope and writeScope cannot be set or seen, though ADR-0084 declares the record-scope column
body:
Filing gate ②: a maintainer ruling, carried out as child 1 of the nine that #26059's ruling (Q3) names. ⛔ Not a claim.

A customer admin cannot set or see a permission set's record scope from the console. The matrix in Setup → Permission Sets and Studio → Access offers C / R / U / D / Tr / VA / MA and field read/write, but it has no control for `readScope` / `writeScope` (`own` / `own_and_reports` / `unit` / `unit_and_below` / `org`). The permission-set and position pages do not show the current scope either. The only way to set it today is `PUT /api/v1/meta/permission/:name`. Backend, enterprise resolver and explain all handle scope correctly (33/33 UI scenarios in #26059's run); only the editor is missing.

Part of #26059
Ruling-ref: 6416233738 (https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/26059#issuecomment-6416233738)
Ruling: batch #396 item 1, letter Q1 是 / Q2 不做 / Q3 分拆 / Q4 框架; this card is Q1 = Q3 child 1 (ui, p1). Brief 6415795834, item-by-item reading 6415971852 (item 1).
Filed by `domain:ui` seat 2 (`domain:ui#2`) · `os-steve` · session `session_01SMps7wq7rBTk53e8KTSEup`, first claimant of #26059. Domain, grade and route are triage's on first touch.

**Business reason.** A customer admin who builds or changes a permission set has no way to grant org-structure scope ("own", "own and reports", "my unit", "my unit and below", "whole org") and cannot see what a set already grants. This is the customer-facing entry point of the RBAC + org-structure feature. Without it the feature can only be configured by a developer through the API.

**Reader who acts.** The `domain:ui` execution seat, dispatch step: one os-dev, one PR in `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/` (the matrix editor, plus the permission-set and position pages).

**Spec contract.** None changes. The enum (`ObjectAccessScopeSchema`) and the contradictory-pair refusal (#16870) are already in `@objectstack/spec`. No ADR change: ADR-0084:47 already declares the column.

**Duplicate check.** A local scan of the 1,962 newest issues (all states, #22168–#26181) for `(readScope|writeScope|record scope|access scope).{0,200}(matrix|PermissionMatrix|select|UI|editor)` and the reverse order found 2 hits, neither about this (#23134 related-list binding, #24034 org-page decision). Triage's scan of the 600 newest (6414323834) found none.

## Ruled scope (ruling Q1)

- The permission matrix gains a **read-scope** and a **write-scope** select per object row. Values come from `ObjectAccessScopeSchema` (`packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts:18`).
- The selects are **greyed by the #16870 pairs** that the BASE schema already refuses (`permission.zod.ts:632`): View All beside a read depth, and Modify All beside either depth. The UI mirrors the server's refusal and does not re-implement it.
- The three hierarchy values (`own_and_reports`, `unit`, `unit_and_below`) stay selectable when `hierarchySecurity` is not licensed, with the hint **"requires enterprise; otherwise owner-only"**. Hint source: `packages/spec/src/kernel/platform-capabilities.ts:224` ("ADR-0057 hierarchy scopes ship in the enterprise edition", token `hierarchy-security`). The open runtime fails closed to owner-only.
- `previews/PermissionPreview.tsx` is wired **read-only** into the permission-set and position pages.
- No spec key and no ADR change.

## Anchors (re-read on `origin/main` `83a26c38`)

- `docs/adr/0084-application-builder-information-architecture.md:47`: Access pillar = "a permission **matrix** (roles × objects × CRUD + record scope)". Holds.
- `docs/adr/0090-permission-model-v2-concept-convergence.md:642`: the ObjectUI landing list names "OWD context per object row" and no scope column. Holds.
- `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx`:
  - The modelled columns are at `:272–283`, so the ruling's `:273–283` is off by one.
  - The #6605 ride-through comment for `readScope` / `writeScope` is at `:959–981`; the ruling's `:961–975` falls inside it.
- `packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts`:
  - `:18` `ObjectAccessScopeSchema` holds.
  - `:632` holds: the #16870 refusal sits on the BASE schema and is attached at `:642`.
- `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/PermissionPreview.tsx:78–137` holds:
  - `SCOPE_ORDER` is at `:78` and the `own+reports` / `unit+below` labels at `:80–86`.
  - The write-wider-than-read warning is at `:124–145` and the scope cells at `:261–270`.
  - Today it is registered only as the metadata preview for `permission` / `profile` (`previews/index.ts:85–86`).
- Permission-set page: `PermissionMatrixEditPage`, mounted from `ui/packages/app-shell/src/services/builtinComponents.tsx:21` and Studio `studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx:216`. Position page: `metadata-admin/ResourceEditPage.tsx`, which already imports `PositionHoldersSection` (`:154`).
- Open-edition fail-closed: `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-service.ts:2084–2085` (`resolveOwnerScopeIds`: with no hierarchy resolver it returns `[me]`). The ruling cited `sharing-service.ts:377`, which on both `cdd4eea9` and `83a26c38` is a phantom-anchor notice comment. Corrected.

**Note for the dev (found while verifying, not a new rule).** The bulk row arms interact with the new selects:
- "None" replaces the row with `{}` (`:969–971`), which drops any scope. A test pins this: `PermissionMatrixEditor.bulkMergeKeys.test.tsx`.
- "All" grants VA + MA while scopes ride through (`:984–987`). On a row that has a scope, that makes a pair the BASE schema refuses.

Say in the PR how the greying covers these two paths. A behaviour question goes on this card and links the ruling.

## Expected / acceptance

- Every object row of the matrix, in Setup → Permission Sets and in Studio → Access, has a Read scope and a Write scope select. Each offers the five `ObjectAccessScopeSchema` values plus "not set". A chosen value saves and reloads unchanged.
- Ticking View All disables the read-scope select, and ticking Modify All disables both selects. No save from the matrix sends a pair the BASE schema refuses (#16870).
- On a deployment without `hierarchy-security`, the three hierarchy values stay selectable and carry the hint "requires enterprise; otherwise owner-only".
- The permission-set and position pages show the current read/write scope per object read-only, through `PermissionPreview`.
- Keys the matrix does not author still ride through a save; the #6605 pins stay green.
- Tests cover rendering, greying, the unlicensed hint and the save round-trip. No change under `packages/spec` and no ADR change.
